Random sampling counters automation bias by ensuring that not all investigations are based solely on high-risk signals generated by algorithms. By incorporating a random sample into the fraud detection process, inspectors are encouraged to critically evaluate cases rather than relying blindly on algorithmic results. This approach helps to mitigate the risk of discrimination by allowing for a more balanced selection of cases for investigation.

Regarding the AI Act duties for high-risk providers, the use of random sampling is relevant because high-risk AI systems are required to identify and mitigate reasonably foreseeable risks, including potential discrimination. The random sample can serve as a control tool to monitor these risks, ensuring compliance with the AI Act's requirements for transparency and accountability in the deployment of high-risk AI systems.
